description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: SIX, not three - BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: CS pulled UP, SCLK and MOSI to ground, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: same, because with OE disabled the buffer outputs are Hi-Z and it is then the DAC's SCLK/DIN/SYNC that float - which is the state these were bought for and the three cable-side pulls do not reach. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. CABLE-SIDE CS PULLS TO 3V3: pulled to 5V it drives 430uA continuously through the unpowered ESP32's input clamp in the design's NORMAL resting state, and the node sits at ~0.7V so 'CS idle high' is not even achieved. DAC-SIDE CS PULLS TO AVDD (the LM317's 5.21V), not bus +5V - a pull-up belongs on its consumer's rail, and on the bus rail a reversed ribbon reaches the DAC's SYNC pin and turns a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure *** ONE OF THE SIX IS NOT PLACEABLE YET: 3V3 EXISTS ONLY AT THE INSTRUMENT END. *** The module makes +/-12V, bus +5V and DAC AVDD, and the umbilical carries no 3V3, so the cable-side CS pull is either an instrument-end part or it needs a rail this board does not have. Lay out the other five; hold that one until digital-and-supervision.md's Still open settles which end it sits at

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE. 100R, not 220R. *** 2m OF CAT5 IS A 100-OHM TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), NOT AN RC CORNER *** - three reviewers agreed independently that the old RC derivation was simply the wrong model, so do not re-derive this one from a corner frequency. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. ORDER CODE IS SP0504BAHTG AND IT IS SOT-23-5, NOT SOT-23-6 [SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table, package outlines pp.6-7]; SP0505BAHTG is the SOT-23-6 part and brings a fifth channel if one is wanted. *** THE PART HAS NO PULSE RATING AT ALL. *** Eight pages carry no I_PP, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform, no surge curve and no theta-JA: it is ESD-rated only (IEC 61000-4-2, 20kV contact / 30kV air). What it does specify is a steady-state ceiling - package dissipation 0.225 W [Abs Max p.2, corroborated 'PD@70degC .225W' p.7]. SO A SUSTAINED FAULT IS NOT SURVIVED BY A BIGGER ARRAY; the fix is a series resistor or a resettable element. ALL FOUR CHANNELS SHARE ONE COMMON PIN (pin 2), so a single array cannot straddle PWR_GND and DIG_GND - which is why U-TVS-SPI and U-TVS-CHAIN stay two packages. THE ARRAY IS EFFECTIVELY UNI-DIRECTIONAL: the -0.8V negative clamp is a forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee. Fine for 0-3.3V SPI; MUST NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node. 30 pF per channel is high for a modern array - against 2 m of Cat5 and R-SPI-SER that is ~29 ns of edge on a 250 ns half-period at 2 MHz, acceptable, and it is the only TVS term in the umbilical edge budget. DO NOT RE-PROPOSE onsemi ESD7104: it is a clean 4-channel 5V array on paper and ships only in UDFN10 and WDFNW10, leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy - as was SP3012-06UTG before it. Two parts have now been rejected for that one reason

description: The umbilical's connector on the main board: CBL-UMB-PATCH from the etherCON's rear socket plugs in here
notes: PINOUT IS umbilical-pinmap, PIN N = etherCON PIN N: CBL-UMB-PATCH is straight, so 'J-UMB pin N' on any page is the same conductor as J-UMBILICAL pin N. WHERE: the main board's tail end, as far in as the patch lead's bend needs - mechanical/drc.echo 'J-UMB on the main board, the patch lead at its bend radius'. D-REVSHUNT and U-TVS-SPI sit at it. RATING: one contact carries +12V (umbilical-current) and one PWR_GND. Rate the contacts above the module's current limit (R-ILIM, hardware/module/umbilical-load-switch/), not the typical draw - a short is carried at the limit until the load switch times out. LATCHING, so the lead cannot back out. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: the envelope fits a 1.25mm-pitch latching family; the envelope is from memory too]. Decided at M4 with the part, together with CBL-UMB-PATCH's housing

description: Inside the tail: the etherCON's rear RJ45 socket to J-UMB on the main board
notes: STRAIGHT, pin N to pin N, T568B at the RJ45 - it has no pin map of its own, so it cannot disagree with umbilical-pinmap. KEEP THE PAIRS TWISTED up to the housing: the pairing is the argument (hardware/interfaces/spi-link/spi-link.md), and this lead is the last stretch of the same line as CABLE-UMB.
